review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the OAI Lean sources for uses of the projection lemmas (cfc_projection_zero, positiveCut_projection, cutoff_projection), cornerCFC_eq and traceTwoNorm_real_smul. The projection lemmas have side conditions and are used only by `rw`, so I don't recommend making them simp. The one concrete gap is that `cornerCFC` has no unfolding or normal-form lemma. cornerCFC_eq has hypotheses and a different shape, so it doesn't fill that gap. I did not read the other files that use cornerCFC, and I can't run Lean. The proposed lemma is therefore untested.

findings.excerpt:
def cornerCFC {u : D} (hu : IsStarProjection u) (x : D) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : D :=
  (cfc f (ProjectionCorner.compress hu x) : ProjectionCorner hu)
findings.problem: `cornerCFC` is a plain def with no unfolding or coercion lemma, so it isn't part of any simp interface. The file has to drop to `change` and a `show … from rfl` rewrite to expose `cfc f (compress hu x)`. This happens in cornerCFC_eq (`change cornerCFC hu x f - f 0 • u = …`) and in cornerCFC_approx, which restates the long subtype-coerced expression twice (lines 249–252). The only rewrite lemma, cornerCFC_eq, needs `IsSelfAdjoint x` and a continuity hypothesis. It also rewrites into a different ambient form with `(1-u)`, so it can't serve as a general simp normal form.
findings.proposed_change: Add an unconditional lemma `cornerCFC_def : cornerCFC hu x f = ((cfc f (ProjectionCorner.compress hu x) : ProjectionCorner hu) : D) := rfl`, or an equivalent simp lemma, and perhaps a difference lemma `cornerCFC hu x f - cornerCFC hu x g = ((cfc f c - cfc g c : ProjectionCorner hu) : D)`. Then cornerCFC_approx can be `simp only [cornerCFC_def, ← Subtype.coe_sub …]` or `rw`, instead of the `change … rw [← show … from rfl]` block. Alternatively, mark `cornerCFC` `@[reducible]` or give it a coe-based statement so the defeq `change` steps are unnecessary.
findings.benefit: Readers and downstream users of cornerCFC (the five other files that mention it) get a stable rewrite target instead of repeating `change` with large explicit terms. This keeps the corner functional-calculus API from depending on definitional unfolding.
